title: [Bug]: worker_threads sized from host cores, ignoring the container CPU quota
body:
### Reproduction link or steps

The bug needs a Linux cgroup CPU limit, which the REPL and StackBlitz cannot express, so here is a self-contained Docker reproduction. The host below has 4 physical cores.

`probe.mjs`:

```js
import { readFileSync, readdirSync } from 'node:fs'
import 'rolldown'   // no build is run; the import alone is enough

const threads = readdirSync('/proc/self/task').map((task) =>
  readFileSync(`/proc/self/task/${task}/comm`, 'utf8').trim(),
)
console.log(readFileSync('/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max', 'utf8').trim(),
  '->', threads.filter((c) => c === 'rolldown-worker').length, 'rolldown-worker')
```

```sh
npm i rolldown@1.1.3

# A: limited to 2 CPUs
docker run --rm --cpus=2 -v "$PWD:/app" -w /app node:22-alpine node probe.mjs
# B: no limit (control)
docker run --rm          -v "$PWD:/app" -w /app node:22-alpine node probe.mjs
```

Actual output:

```
A:  200000 100000  -> 6 rolldown-worker     # quota = 2 CPUs
B:  max 100000     -> 6 rolldown-worker     # unlimited
```

A and B are identical, so the quota has no effect on the pool size. 6 = `4 host physical cores * 3 / 2`.

### What is expected?

`worker_threads` should be derived from the CPU allocation the process actually has (the cgroup quota), not from the host's physical core count. Arm A above should size its pool from 2 CPUs, not from the host's 4.

Measured with `num_cpus` 1.17.0 — same binary, same host (4 physical / 8 logical cores):

| | `--cpus=2` | no limit |
|---|---|---|
| `num_cpus::get_physical()` (currently used) | 4 | 4 |
| `num_cpus::get()` | 2 | 8 |
| `std::thread::available_parallelism()` | 2 | 8 |

`get_physical()` is the only one of the three that is blind to the quota.

Note that simply swapping in `num_cpus::get()` would also change behaviour on unconstrained hosts (4 -> 8 here, so `worker_threads` 6 -> 12), because it counts logical CPUs. If the `* 3 / 2`-on-physical-cores heuristic is intentional, the smaller fix is to clamp it by the quota rather than replace the source, e.g.

```rust
let cores = num_cpus::get_physical().min(
    std::thread::available_parallelism().map(|p| p.get()).unwrap_or(usize::MAX),
);
// cores * 3 / 2
```

### What is actually happening?

`crates/rolldown_binding/src/lib.rs` sizes the tokio runtime at module init with:

```rust
.unwrap_or(num_cpus::get_physical() * 3 / 2)
```

`num_cpus::get_physical()` parses `/proc/cpuinfo`, which is not namespaced, so inside a container it reports the **host's** cores and never consults the cgroup quota. Its sibling `num_cpus::get()` in the same file does consult it.

Measured, rolldown 1.1.3:

| environment | host physical cores | cgroup quota | `rolldown-worker` threads |
|---|---|---|---|
| docker `--cpus=2` | 4 | 2 CPUs | 6 |
| docker, no limit (control) | 4 | unlimited | 6 |
| production container | 48 | 24 CPUs | 72 |

Every row equals `host_physical_cores * 3 / 2`. The 24-CPU production container gets a 72-thread pool.

Because the runtime is built in `#[napi_derive::module_init]`, this is paid on **import**, even when no build is ever run.

### System Info

```Shell
Reproduction host:
  OS:       Ubuntu 25.10, Docker, image node:22-alpine
  Node:     v22.22.0 (host) / v22.x (container)
  rolldown: 1.1.3 (@rolldown/binding-linux-x64-musl)
  physical cores: 4 (8 logical)
  arm A: cpu.max = "200000 100000" (2 CPUs)   -> 6 rolldown-worker
  arm B: cpu.max = "max 100000"    (no limit) -> 6 rolldown-worker

Production container where this was first hit:
  OS:       Alpine Linux v3.24 (musl)
  Node:     v22.23.2
  rolldown: 1.1.3
  host physical cores: 48
  cgroup cpu.max: "2400000 100000" (24 CPUs)
  observed: 72 rolldown-worker threads
```

### Any additional comments?

Context on how this was hit, since the cost is easy to miss.

Directus depends on rolldown and imports it statically in its extension manager, but only selects it behind an opt-in flag that defaults to false (`directus/directus`, `api/package.json:183`, `api/src/extensions/manager.ts:40` and `:587`). rolldown is therefore never called, yet every Directus process still paid 72 permanently idle threads at import.

With several Node processes per container this exhausted the cgroup `pids.max` (864 of 1000). The first thing to fail was an unrelated `pthread_create` — inside argon2, during password verification, which began throwing `Threading failure`. Login was down in production while the rest of the API served normally.

Suggested fix: clamp the default by the cgroup quota (see "What is expected?").

Workaround: set `ROLLDOWN_WORKER_THREADS`. Verified — `--cpus=2` with `ROLLDOWN_WORKER_THREADS=1` gives 1 thread. Note it must be a real process environment variable, since it is read via `std::env::var` at module init, so a value in an application's own `.env`-style config will not reach it.
